text:
samir: Heads-up — last night we had a noisy streak of GPU Xid / ECC corrected spikes in us-west-2 causing node drains. I muted the alert but want to propose a safer automation before we enable auto-drain again.

jia: Ack. Can you paste the alert that fired and a short timeline?

samir: Timeline: 03:12 multiple Xid 31 from node-gpu-17, 03:13 driver restart, 03:15 kubelet marked OOM/killed pods -> drain by oncall script. Pattern repeated ~5x across 4 nodes in 40m. No permanent hardware failure detected yet.

morgan: Ugh noise. Were ECC corrected counts increasing steadily or bursty? That's the key to avoid false positives.

samir: Mostly bursty corrected errors + 1 soft-failure (nvml reported Xid). ECC corrected delta per-minute spiked >200 for a minute then dropped.

eva: For automation we should require 2 independent signals before cordon+drain: (1) sustained Xid or ECC delta over a sliding window, AND (2) either driver crash or repeated nvml process restarts. Otherwise just taint+notify.

ryan: +1. Also want exponential backoff to avoid flapping: mark node as "under-investigation" for N minutes after a remediation attempt and suppress further auto actions.

jia: Proposed policy sketch:
- Alert rule (prometheus) -> create a "gpu_flaky" signal when: Xid_count_rate > 20/min over 5m OR ECC_corrected_rate > 100/min over 3m.
- If gpu_flaky && driver_restarts >=1 in 10m -> auto cordon+drain with graceful eviction (30s grace) and annotate node: gpu-failure=investigating
- Else if gpu_flaky only -> add taint gpu=flaky:NoSchedule + create ticket and escalate oncall.
- After drain, run a health-probe job that runs `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total --format=csv` and `dmesg` check; if probe passes, uncordon with a replacement cooldown of 60m.

samir: Sounds good. Can we include a device-level fence step for Slurm nodes? For Slurm we need `scontrol update NodeName=node state=drain Reason="gpu-flake auto"` before kube drain, otherwise running batches get killed ungracefully.

morgan: Right — order for hybrid clusters: 1) annotate/taint to prevent new pods/jobs, 2) scontrol drain for slurm, 3) kubectl drain. Keep the client-visible downtime minimized.

ops-bot: Reminder: deploy pipeline requires a feature flag for auto-drain. Current flag: `autodrain.gpu.enabled=false`.

jia: Example alert snippet for Prometheus (draft):
```yaml
- alert: GPUBurstErrors
  expr: increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_total[5m]) > 20 or increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_corrected[3m]) > 100
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood.infradev/runbooks/gpu-flake
```

eva: And the remediation playbook (high level):
- Checknode script collects: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,INFORMATION`, `journalctl -u nvidia* -b`, `dmesg | tail -n200`
- If driver crash detected -> trigger cordon+drain, kick off a node-level systemd restart sequence on driver + kubelet health check
- If node recovers -> uncordon after cooldown and leave a marker `gpu.flake.cooldown_until=<ts>`
- If node fails health-probe 2x in 12h -> mark for replacement and open HW ticket (annotate with `gpu-replace=true`)

samir: Edge-case: what about flaky nodes that intermittently pass the probe? We should only auto-replace after repeated failed probes (2-3 attempts) and also consult our spare capacity so we don't rip multiple nodes at once in a region.

ryan: We should also add cost-control: if region spare capacity < 10% then demote auto-replace to manual approval and instead route traffic to cheaper fallback model variants to keep latency/SLOs.

morgan: Implementation notes:
- Add a small controller (python/golang) that subscribes to Prometheus alerts via Alertmanager webhook and does stateful debouncing per-node.
- Keep state in k8s CRD `GPUHealthStatus` storing last_actions and counters (but the final artifact will be annotations on Node).
- Use leader election to avoid concurrent remediations.

jia: Testing plan:
- Unit tests for debouncing logic
- Integration env: run synthetic workload that emits Xid/ECC metrics via a test exporter and assert desired actions (taint vs drain vs replace)
- Canary rollout behind feature flag on a small pool (5 nodes) for 2 weeks

eva: Ops runbook additions: quick commands
- taint: `kubectl taint node N gpu=flaky:NoSchedule --overwrite`
- slurm drain: `scontrol update NodeName=N State=drain Reason=auto_gpu_flake`
- cordon+drain: `kubectl cordon N && kubectl drain N --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 --timeout=600s`

samir: I'll draft the controller spec and alert rules, then open a PR with the feature flag and the canary config. Can someone own the runbook updates?

morgan: I'll take runbook + integration tests. Jia can you own AlertManager rules and oncall paging tweaks?

jia: Yup. I'll also add a mute window config per-region so we can tune thresholds regionally.

ops-bot: Action items created: #INC-1428 (design PR), #INC-1429 (prometheus rule), #INC-1430 (runbook).

samir: Thanks folks. One last ask: make sure telemetry includes post-remediation success/failure events so we can measure false-positive rate and time-to-replace.

ryan: Will add metrics: `gpu_auto_remediation_attempt_total{outcome=success|failed|recovered}` and `gpu_auto_remediation_backoff_seconds`

morgan: Cool. I'll start a draft PR in infra/autodrain and tag everyone. :thumbsup:
